_comment: Translucent silicone rubber (cured PDMS, uncoloured): the milky, soft, slightly tacky moulded rubber of kitchen utensils and bakeware, baby-bottle teats, seals and phone cases. SUBSURFACE: its look is light passing into it and spreading, so thin parts glow and edges soften; it is not see-through like a clear plastic. Satin moulded finish. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): scratches (overlay 1, damage), fingerprints (silicone picks up grease), and dust as a deposit (Phase10; silicone is notorious for holding lint), gated by the Grime mask in the row's order. Built by the Phase11 batch.
name: Silicone_Translucent_Clean_Base_s01_v01

sources.why: specular_ior 1.41 (PDMS silicone is 1.40-1.43); a milky near-neutral body (base 0.82, 0.82, 0.80; subsurface colour 0.86, 0.86, 0.84), author-light so a Creator can tint it; subsurface_weight 1 and subsurface_radius 0.01 m with a near-neutral scale (1.0, 1.0, 0.95): uncoloured translucent silicone diffuses light about a centimetre, so thin parts glow but nothing is seen through; roughness 0.4 for a satin moulded finish. Physically Based has no silicone entry.
